html:
SMTO-BOOT-0050 — SMTO couldn't reopen your saved work

GUID: f0436b8a-9c45-45d4-a387-363f9a654852
Slug: startup-state-restore-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO stopped while loading your saved conversations and Tasks because a step that reads them didn't finish safely. This alone doesn't mean your data is damaged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure only one SMTO is running: close any other window running ./startup.sh, and stop the installed app if it's also open. Two copies opening the same saved data can get in each other's way while it loads.
  2. Select Start again on this screen if you see it, or start SMTO the way you normally do. Try this once. Starting again repeats the loading step without repeating any of your earlier work.
  3. If you recently installed a different version of SMTO, tell the person who manages SMTO which version you used before. The installed version is one of the first things they'll check when saved work won't load.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations and Tasks appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the error reference, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete, move or edit SMTO's data folder; it holds the work they need to recover.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because a runtime-state component (agent_runtime.runtime_state) raised an error that has no more specific catalog identity while restoring or taking ownership of saved state.

What this means

  • A restore, schema, manifest or ownership condition prevented initialization. The failed stage narrows the operation; this category alone does not establish corruption or authorize deleting state.

Why this can happen

  • A restore, schema, manifest or ownership condition prevented initialization. The failed stage narrows the operation; this category alone does not establish corruption or authorize deleting state.

How to diagnose it

  • The controller could not establish a usable runtime state during startup.
  • The controller restores and seals its saved state without errors.

How to fix it

  • Read the failed stage and error in Technical details or the Server log (for example a state-preparation helper process that stalled or exited), confirm no other Server uses the same AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR, and check the installed version and host memory and disk headroom before restarting. If recovery is needed, stop the Server, take a copy with aor backup-export, and keep the state directory and occurrence ID intact.
  • Preserve the runtime directory and occurrence ID. Check the failed stage and installed version, confirm no other controller owns this state, and use the documented backup/recovery workflow if recovery is required.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The controller restores and seals its saved state without errors.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
